title: payments-api p99 latency 4.2s, checkout timeouts
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=payments-api alert=HighLatencyP99
p99 latency 4.2s (threshold 800ms) for 10m on /v2/charges
WARN  c.z.h.pool.HikariPool - HikariPool-1 - Thread starvation or clock leap detected (housekeeper delta=1m2s)
ERROR o.h.e.j.s.SqlExceptionHelper - HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
root_cause: A slow analytics query (missing index on charges.merchant_id) held connections for 20s+ and starved the HikariCP pool of 20 connections.
worked: Killed the long-running analytics queries with pg_terminate_backend and moved the report to the read replica
notes: Analytics team now runs reports against payments-db-replica-1 only.

title: orders-worker Kafka consumer lag 180k on orders.created
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=orders-worker alert=KafkaConsumerLagHigh
consumer_group=orders-worker topic=orders.created lag=181,402 (threshold 10,000)
ERROR o.a.k.c.c.i.ConsumerCoordinator - [orders-worker] Offset commit failed on partition orders.created-7
ERROR c.s.orders.OrderHandler - Failed to deserialize message at offset 9918273: Unexpected character ('<' (code 60))
root_cause: A poison message (HTML error page published by a misconfigured upstream proxy) on partition 7 made the handler throw and retry forever, blocking that partition.
worked: Skipped the poison offset on partition 7 with kafka-consumer-groups --reset-offsets --shift-by 1 and sent the raw message to orders.created.dlq
failed: Scaled orders-worker from 12 to 24 replicas: did not help because the topic has 12 partitions, extra consumers sat idle and lag kept growing
notes: Follow-up: handler now routes undeserializable messages to the DLQ after 3 attempts.

title: auth-service 401 spike, users logged out across web and mobile
alert:
[FIRING] sev1 service=auth-service alert=Auth401Rate
401 rate 38% (threshold 2%) on /oauth/introspect
WARN  c.s.auth.JwtVerifier - Signature verification failed: no key found for kid=2026-09-26-a
INFO  c.s.auth.JwksCache - JWKS cache hit, age=3h57m
root_cause: Signing keys were rotated at 09:00 but auth-service pods cached the old JWKS for 4 hours, so tokens signed with the new key were rejected.
worked: Called POST /admin/jwks/refresh on every auth-service pod to force a JWKS reload
Reduced JWKS cache TTL from 4h to 10m
failed: Rolled back the key rotation: made it worse, because tokens already issued with the new key were then rejected too, and the 401 rate rose to 61% for 8 minutes
notes: Key rotation runbook now requires a JWKS refresh step before switching the active key.

title: payments-api connection pool exhausted, 34% of charges failing
alert:
[FIRING] sev1 service=payments-api alert=ChargeErrorRate
error rate 34% on POST /v2/charges (threshold 1%)
ERROR o.h.e.j.s.SqlExceptionHelper - HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
ERROR c.s.p.ChargeController - Charge failed: CannotCreateTransactionException
FATAL: sorry, too many clients already (payments-db-primary)
root_cause: The 02:50 deploy raised payments-api from 8 to 16 replicas with maxPoolSize 20 each, so 320 connections hit payments-db-primary, which allows max_connections=300. New connections were refused.
worked: Scaled payments-api back to 8 replicas (kubectl scale deploy/payments-api --replicas=8), errors cleared within 4 minutes
Lowered HikariCP maximumPoolSize from 20 to 12 so 16 replicas fit under max_connections
failed: Restarted all payments-api pods at once with kubectl rollout restart: every pod reconnected at the same moment, payments-db-primary hit max_connections immediately and the outage got worse, a 20-minute cascade with checkout fully down
notes: Rule of thumb now: replicas x maxPoolSize must stay under 80% of max_connections. Never restart all payments pods at once during a pool incident.

title: checkout-web 502s from CDN after release 2026.10.19
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=checkout-web alert=Edge5xxRate
CDN 502 rate 12% on /checkout/*
next.js: Error: Cannot find module './chunks/4132.js'
upstream checkout-web: readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
root_cause: The release deployed new HTML before the matching static chunks finished uploading to the CDN bucket, so users got pages that referenced missing JS chunks.
worked: Re-ran the static asset upload job, then purged the CDN cache for /_next/static/*
failed: Purged the entire CDN cache first: origin traffic spiked 9x and checkout-web pods were OOM-killed, adding 15 minutes of downtime
notes: Pipeline now uploads assets before switching traffic. Purge only /_next/static/*, never the whole CDN.

title: notifications email backlog, SES throttling
alert:
[FIRING] sev3 service=notifications alert=EmailQueueDepth
queue=email-outbound depth=48,210 (threshold 5,000)
WARN  c.s.n.SesSender - Throttling: Maximum sending rate exceeded (rate=14/s)
root_cause: A marketing campaign was sent through the transactional email queue and hit the SES sending rate limit of 14 emails per second.
worked: Paused the marketing campaign job and moved it to the bulk queue with its own rate limit
notes: Requested an SES rate increase to 50/s.

title: search-api timeouts, OpenSearch cluster yellow
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=search-api alert=SearchLatency
p95 3.8s on /search (threshold 600ms)
OpenSearch cluster health: yellow, unassigned_shards=14
[o.o.c.r.a.DiskThresholdMonitor] high disk watermark [90%] exceeded on node os-data-2
root_cause: Old daily indices were never deleted because the ISM retention policy was detached during an upgrade, so os-data-2 filled to 91% and shards could not be allocated.
worked: Deleted product-events indices older than 30 days and reattached the ISM retention policy
Shards reallocated and the cluster went green within 12 minutes
failed: Restarted os-data-2: shards started relocating, which made latency worse for 10 minutes and did not free any disk
notes: Added an alert on disk usage at 75%.

title: orders-worker lag again on orders.created after schema change
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=orders-worker alert=KafkaConsumerLagHigh
consumer_group=orders-worker topic=orders.created lag=96,117
ERROR c.s.orders.OrderHandler - Failed to deserialize message at offset 10442817: Unknown field 'gift_wrap' in OrderCreatedV3
root_cause: The storefront team shipped OrderCreatedV3 with a new field before orders-worker was updated, and strict deserialization rejected every new message.
worked: Deployed orders-worker 3.14.2 with the V3 schema (FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES disabled); lag drained in 25 minutes
failed: Scaled orders-worker replicas up: same as INC-2027, more consumers than partitions does nothing for a blocking error
Reset the consumer group to latest: skipped 96k orders that then had to be replayed by hand
notes: Schema registry now enforces backward compatibility on orders.created.

title: payments-api pool timeouts during refund batch
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=payments-api alert=ChargeErrorRate
error rate 6% on POST /v2/charges
ERROR o.h.e.j.s.SqlExceptionHelper - HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
INFO  c.s.p.RefundBatchJob - Processing batch 14/60 (2,000 refunds)
root_cause: The monthly refund batch job runs inside payments-api and held 15 of 20 pool connections for long transactions.
worked: Paused the refund batch with POST /admin/jobs/refund-batch/pause; charge errors cleared in 2 minutes
Moved the refund batch to its own deployment with a separate pool of 5 connections
notes: Second pool-exhaustion incident on payments-api in 3 weeks (see INC-2041).

title: auth-service login latency, Redis session store evictions
alert:
[FIRING] sev2 service=auth-service alert=LoginLatency
p95 2.1s on /login (threshold 400ms)
redis-sessions: evicted_keys rising 4,000/min, used_memory 99.8% of maxmemory (2gb)
root_cause: A bug in the remember-me flow set session TTL to 365 days instead of 30, so the Redis session store filled up and started evicting active sessions.
worked: Hotfixed remember-me TTL back to 30 days and ran a script to cap existing keys at 30 days with EXPIRE
Increased redis-sessions maxmemory to 4gb as a buffer
failed: Ran FLUSHDB on redis-sessions: logged out every user at once and caused a login stampede that took auth-service p95 to 9s
notes: Never FLUSHDB the session store in production.
